statement: A cube-shaped box with no lid is opened out flat in one piece. Each face is a 3 cm by 3 cm square. What is the area of the flat piece, in square centimetres?

choices.misconception: I found the area of only one square face, $3 \times 3 = 9$.
I multiplied the number of faces by the side length, $5 \times 3 = 15$, instead of by the area of a face.
I counted only the four side faces and forgot the bottom of the box, $4 \times 9 = 36$.
I counted six faces as if the box had a lid, $6 \times 9 = 54$.

hints: How many faces does a cube box without a lid have?
Opening the box out does not change the cardboard, so the flat piece has the same faces as the box. Count those faces, then find the area of one face.
The box has a bottom and four sides, so 5 square faces. Each face has area $3 \times 3 = 9$ square centimetres. Multiply 5 by 9.

solutions.reliable: A cube has 6 faces; with no lid the box has 5: a bottom and four sides. Unfolding keeps every face, so the flat piece is 5 squares. Each square is $3 \times 3 = 9$ square centimetres, so the area is $5 \times 9 = 45$. The transferable idea: a net has exactly the faces of the solid, no more and no fewer.

whyOnTest: It checks that a net is made of the solid's faces, here with one face missing, joined to a simple area calculation.
